title: The Boy and the Thieves
summary: A clever twelve-year-old boy named Ali was walking through an isolated lane on the outskirts of Baghdad, carrying a small clay water jug....
full_text:
A clever twelve-year-old boy named Ali was walking through an isolated lane on the outskirts of Baghdad, carrying a small clay water jug. He noticed three notorious thieves lurking in the ruins of an ancient cistern, waiting to rob lone travelers.

Realizing that if he ran, the thieves would pursue and rob him, Ali devised a brilliant ruse. He sat upon the stone lip of the deep well, buried his face in his hands, and began wailing with loud, heartbreaking lamentations!

The three thieves crept out from the shadows, curious and greedy. Their leader asked: 'Why are you weeping so bitterly, boy?'

Ali sniffled and sobbed: 'Alas! My master, the wealthiest jeweler of the bazaar, gave me a magnificent golden goblet studded with emeralds to wash at this spring. As I leaned over, my foot slipped, and the golden goblet tumbled to the bottom of the deep well! If I return without it, my master will have me beaten with forty lashes!'

The thieves’ eyes gleamed with avarice: a golden goblet with emeralds at the bottom of a shallow well!

The three cutpurses immediately stripped off their cloaks, boots, and weapons, leaving them upon the grass, and scrambled down the slippery stones into the dark, muddy water of the well, groping frantically in the muck.

The moment the last thief was at the bottom of the pit, young Ali sprang to his feet!

He gathered all three rich cloaks, their boots, their heavy money belts filled with stolen gold, and ran like a deer to the city gates, delivering the loot directly to the Chief of the Watch!

The guards arrived at the well and hauled the three shivering, muddy thieves up by a rope, throwing them into chains amidst the laughter of all Baghdad, praising the boy who had conquered three cutpurses with nothing but his quick wits.
moral: Quick wit and psychological cunning can outsmart the most hardened cutpurses.
